cohort: The study included 244 synovial sarcoma cases born 1978-2015 and diagnosed 1988-2015 in California, along with 12,200 controls frequency-matched on year of birth.
finding: Synovial sarcoma was more frequent in Hispanics, and higher birth weight was a risk factor in Hispanics, while first-born children had the highest risk of disease.
birth_weight: Higher birth weight was a risk factor, with each 500g increase associated with a 22% increased risk in Hispanics.
